design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 0 (service_billing_and_collections, env_0042 Lakeshore Power & Light)

[0] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py <diff> --task 0, printed): {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4, 6]}. Assignment: reconnection order charge 6, sustained-outage credit 6, reconnection card payment 5, late payment charge 4 -> multiset {4,5,6,6} = draw.

[1] Why this is a good test. A residential customer whose power was cut yesterday asks only to be reconnected today. To do it correctly the agent must read out of the reconnection policy that an order that rests on payment waits on card, pay station cash or energy assistance payments since the disconnection covering 'the reconnection payment amount', then read the payment policy and discover that amount itself waits on two state-due postings nobody mentioned: the late payment charge on the most recent bill (grace ended 2026-09-27, no charge carries its bill id) and the automatic sustained-outage credit for the 29.6-hour outage of 2026-09-08 (no credit carries its outage id). Each of the four writes carries its own multi-factor computation over 14 months of ledger plus meter and deposit records. Difficulty comes from discovering the tree and getting four numbers exactly right, not from tool choice: there is one tool per problem.

[2] Scope (Principle C). Already occupied: nothing (task 0 is first). Claimed here: service_ext_late_charge_assessment (service_late_payment_charge, tool post_late_payment_charge_a575fa01), service_ext_auto_sustained_outage_credit (service_outage_credit sustained_outage, grant_sustained_outage_credit_20084a33), service_ext_reconnection_card_payment (service_payment by card, take_card_payment_dce85fc7, owner=user), service_ext_reconnection_order_charge (service_reconnection + service_reconnection_charge, issue_reconnection_order_52263bc7). Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts [5,4,4]): the chronic-outage credit (service_outage_credit chronic_outage), the prior-balance transfer (service_program_debit/credit) and a business customer's bank-draft payment that heads off a disconnection notice - none of them overlaps a policy, tool or main dependency chain of this task.
Design note on the customer-owned tool: the blueprint names stop-service and start-cancellation confirmations as the customer's own writes, but both carry only dates, which the compute DSL cannot produce; the only numeric write a customer makes in person in this product is a payment, so this task's user tool is the customer's in-call card payment (service_payment, unclaimed by every difficulty). Base defect routed around: the base dedup gate confirmation_posted_once binds the confirmation number as an input, but an in-call card payment receives its number only at authorization (a return value); the extended payment policy declares an overwrite of 'Each confirmation number is posted once.' replaced by 'A card payment taken on the call is posted once, under the one confirmation number its authorization produces.'

[3] Problem-tree card.
Root: service_ext_reconnection_order_charge (customer's request 'reconnected today'; on_request).
Edge E1 root -> service_ext_reconnection_card_payment: kind state_gate, gate service_reconnection_rule.reconnection_requirement_met, form state. Prerequisite sentence (root rule): 'A reconnection order that rests on payment is issued only after the card, authorized pay station cash and energy assistance agency payments posted to the agreement since its disconnection date add up to at least the reconnection payment amount.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; XX = a record-visible state (card, pay station cash and agency payment rows on the agreement since last_status_date); no tool/id/code token; hard requirement scoped to a reconnection that rests on payment (the base alternatives - an active arrangement with its down payment received, an active medical certification that requires restoration - stay in force and are restated in the rule). Of those channels only card payments are written by a tool of this difficulty (take_card_payment_dce85fc7; the task-1 tool posts bank drafts, which the rule says do not count), so the state singles out the customer's card payment. Seed falsity: last_status_date 2026-09-28; newest card row 2026-05-28, newest agency row 2026-07-15; nothing since. Owner of the resolving tool: user.
Edge E2 card payment -> service_ext_late_charge_assessment: kind value_input, gate charges_total, form state. Sentence (payment rule, affirmative): 'The reconnection payment amount is fixed only after the agreement carries a late payment charge on its most recent bill once that bill's grace period has ended with part of it unpaid.' Same scope as the late-charge rule (most recent bill only). Falsity: bill 99539ce4-96b2-496e-acc9-6acad864d387 due 2026-09-22, unpaid, no late charge row carries it. Effect: charges_total 185.02 -> 188.10, payment 291.38 -> 293.04.
Edge E3 card payment -> service_ext_auto_sustained_outage_credit: kind value_input, gate credits_total, form state. Sentence (payment rule, negated): 'The reconnection payment amount is not fixed until the agreement carries the sustained-outage credit owed for the most recent outage record at its service address when that record qualifies.' Same scope as the outage rule (the most recent record, when it qualifies). Falsity: outage 53768c09-df38-40b3-b0c7-1f094ef52f3b (29.6 h, equipment failure) has no credit row. Effect: credits_total 1559.96 -> 1702.46, payment 369.99 -> 293.04.
Directions: E2 affirmative ('fixed only after'), E3 negated ('not fixed until'), E1 affirmative ('issued only after').
Topological order: late charge (steps 12-13), sustained-outage credit (14-15), card payment handed over and run by the customer (16-17), reconnection order (18-19). value_input edges = 2 >= max(3-1,1).
Parallel edges E2/E3 commute (run): with the credit first the late charge's unpaid portion is min(168.51, 357.12) = 168.51, the charge stays 3.08, the payment 293.04, terminal DB identical.
Per-edge deletion sensitivity (run): skip late charge -> payment 291.38; skip outage credit -> payment 369.99; skip card payment -> no payment row, balance 369.05 instead of 76.01.
user_scenario never names a late charge, an outage, a credit or a 'first' step; the tools validate nothing.

[4] Base-invariant card.
Late charge (service_late_payment_charge_rule): grace_period_passed (time; anchor service_bills.due_date 2026-09-22; Schedule RS 5 days; exclusive; first permitted 2026-09-28; frozen 2026-09-29 satisfies; 2026-09-27 would fail); one_charge_per_bill (no late charge carries 99539ce4-96b2-496e-acc9-6acad864d387); charge_on_open_agreement (status disconnected is allowed). Income qualification: income_qualified_until 2025-06-30 < due date 2026-09-22, so the income exemption does not apply. No customer-requested meter test exists.
Sustained credit (service_outage_credit_rule + service_chronic_outage_credit): claim_window (anchor restoration 2026-09-10 01:16; 90 days counted from 2026-09-11; inclusive; last day 2026-12-09; frozen day 19); one_credit_per_code_per_outage (no credit carries 53768c09-df38-40b3-b0c7-1f094ef52f3b); one_chronic_credit_per_outage (no chronic credit in 12 months). Not a major event day; cause equipment failure is not excluded.
Payment (service_payments_and_returns): its only gate (confirmation_posted_once) is retired by the declared overwrite; returned-payment restriction: 1 return in 12 months < 2, and a card is accepted anyway.
Reconnection (service_reconnection_rule): reconnection_requirement_met by the step-17 card payment (prior_step evidence); charge_after_restoration - the order restores status before the same call posts the charge. Inherited, unexercised: the medical-waiver and invalid-notice clauses (no medical certification; the 2026-09-14 written notice was valid: past due 331.11 >= 100, oldest unpaid bill due 2026-05-22 >= 30 days, earliest disconnect 2026-09-24, disconnection 2026-09-28 a Monday inside the 30-day validity, door-hanger final notice 2026-09-22 >= 48 h before, no moratorium for non-electric heat). Deposit program: the Residential Reestablishment Deposit has been held (fully secured 2025-12-07, 263.00) since the 2025 disconnection, so its first-installment condition for reconnection is satisfied and no new deposit obligation is owed in this task.

[5] Business-object card. Target agreement 61e0ebe3-1883-4d41-b37e-ea2ac53eb08a (Schedule RS, 418 W 21st St). Late charge object: bill 99539ce4-96b2-496e-acc9-6acad864d387 (only bill past grace without a charge). Outage object: record 53768c09-df38-40b3-b0c7-1f094ef52f3b (most recent record). Payment and reconnection: the agreement itself; the reconnection charge attaches to today's order. Included rows: all 14 bills and every charge/credit enter the balance; the 2025-09-29 late charge (exactly 12 months old) is excluded from the recent-late-charge sum and the late-charge count; the 2025-08-14 outage is outside the 12-month counts; the phone-call final notice of 2026-09-25 is not a door-hanger visit; the 2025-02-11 field order found no tampering.

[6] Factor card (baseline figure = result with only that factor at its fall-through; full-baseline figure = computation document alone).
Late charge (expected 3.08; full baseline 2.53): repeat_lateness_rate - 2 late charges in the repeat-lateness window -> 1.25 x rate (baseline 2.76); autopay_lateness_window (method: window convention) - 3 autopay payments -> lateness counted over 3 months instead of 12 (baseline 3.40); assistance_hardship_share - 2 agency payments -> one half (baseline 4.66); written_notice_surcharge - 2 written notices -> +1.50 (baseline 1.58).
Sustained credit (expected 142.50; full baseline 35.00): qualifying_duration_measure (method, cross-difficulty meter) - 60-minute AMI -> 29.6 h up to 30 h (baseline 112.50); assisted_household_minimum_duration - 12 h (82.50); outage_frequency_increment_hours - 4 records -> 6 h (82.50); outage_cause_base_amount - equipment failure -> 52.50 (125.00); repeat_equipment_failure_increment - 2 failures -> 30.00 (127.50); tenure_outage_credit_cap - 124 months -> cap 175.50 (135.00).
Card payment (expected 293.04; full baseline 344.73): reconnection_history_basis (method) - one reconnection in 24 months -> balance less late charges 12+ months old (286.15); assistance_payment_share 0.6 (421.73); tenure_payment_share 0.9 (314.49); notice_goodfaith_addon +50.00 (243.04); returned_payment_addon +50.00 (243.04).
Reconnection charge (expected 8.85; full baseline 65.00): restoration_path_charge (multi-source, cross-difficulty meter) - remote-capable meter and no tampering finding -> 10.00 (25.35); collection_cycle_assistance_window (method: window anchored on the last reconnection) - 10-month window (5.90); door_hanger_visit_recovery 19.50 (3.00); assistance_charge_share 0.75 (11.80); tenure_charge_share 0.8 (11.06); reestablishment_deposit_share (cross-difficulty deposit) 0.5 (17.70).
Near-misses planted: the late charge of 2025-09-29 (exactly 12 months, out of the recent sum); the 2026-06-28 late charge (3 whole months back, out of the lateness window); the 2025-11-07 agency payment (10 whole months back, out of the assistance window but inside the 12-month counts); the 2025-08-14 vegetation outage; the phone-call final notice; the no-tampering field order; the 2025-08-22 autopay payment.

[7] Persona design. Wendeline Sorbara, 68, retired librarian, apologetic and anxious; volunteers only 'power shut off yesterday, reconnect today, can pay by debit card'. Given only when asked: phone 6164158823, SSN last four 1764, ZIP 49423, email. Passive reactions: consents when told something must be put on the account first; declines paying off everything; runs the handed-over card payment for exactly the quoted amount and reads back the confirmation number; ends when told the reconnection is ordered. No ask outside gold.

[8] Standard solution. Locate (phone) -> verify (phone + SSN4) -> read agreement, bills, charges, credits, notices, outages, meter, meter field orders, deposits and deposit transactions -> post late charge 3.08 on 99539ce4-96b2-496e-acc9-6acad864d387 -> post sustained-outage credit 142.50 on 53768c09-df38-40b3-b0c7-1f094ef52f3b -> hand over card payment; customer pays 293.04 -> issue reconnection order (8.85, remote, standard_hours).

[9] Verification run (round 2, real tools replayed on initial_state with check_compute primitives): late charge 3.08; outage credit 142.50; payment 293.04 (balance 360.20 at handling time); reconnection charge 8.85; terminal balance 76.01. Per-factor baseline figures as in [6]. Gates: the full block re-run after round 2.

[10] Draft recomputation from visible context only: the reconnection rule's prerequisite sentence (a reconnection that rests on payment waits on card, pay station cash and agency payments since disconnection) sends the agent to the reconnection payment rule; its two prerequisite sentences name the late payment charge on the most recent bill and the sustained-outage credit for the most recent outage record when it qualifies; the reads show the 2026-09-01 bill without a charge and the 29.6 h record without a credit; recomputing each rule from the rows gives 3.08, 142.50, 293.04, 8.85 - identical to gold.

[11] Revision log - rework round 2 (audit audits/policy_task/service_billing_and_collections/, revision 1).
F-1 (symptom: the reconnection gate dropped base alternatives and non-card payments without declaration; root cause: no overwrite for the payment-requirement clause) -> the reconnection rule now scopes its prerequisite sentence to a reconnection that rests on payment, restates the base arrangement/medical alternatives, counts card, pay station cash and agency payments, excludes returnable channels with its reason, and declares the overwrite of the base payment-requirement clause. Propagated to the edge condition, E1 why_false/evidence, gold step 17/19 texts.
F-3 (late charge and reconnection charge carried only multiplier 'methods') -> late charge: the autopay multiplier is replaced by a window-convention method (repeat lateness counted over 1/3/12 months by autopay history); reconnection charge: the repeat multiplier is replaced by a window-anchor method (assistance payments counted since the last reconnection / over 6 months after a notice / over 12 months). Values recomputed: late charge 3.21 -> 3.08, payment 293.11 -> 293.04, reconnection charge 6.90 -> 8.85; all factor figures re-run.
Finding 5 (false closure evidence 2026-06-22) -> E1 now cites the 2026-05-28 card row and the 2026-07-15 agency row.
Finding 6 (false factor_trace assertions) -> the agency payment is 90.00 and the standard payment basis 344.73 (both rewritten from the seed and the re-run).
Observations: O-1/O-2 the payment rule's two sentences now carry exactly the scope of the late-charge and outage rules; O-3 late-charge inputs metadata completed; O-4 tampering count also subtracts 'no access' investigations; O-5 deposit-payment wording aligned with the window convention; finding 7 (8.625 tie) disappears with the new figures.
user_scenario: You are Wendeline Sorbara, 68, a retired school librarian who lives alone at 418 W 21st St in Holland, Michigan. Lakeshore Power & Light cut off your electricity yesterday, Monday, and you are calling on Tuesday afternoon because you want the power back on at the house today. You had a rough year after your hours at the library annex ended and you fell behind again, but your pension came in this morning and you are ready to pay by debit card whatever the company needs before it will turn the power back on. You speak warmly but a little anxiously, and you apologise more than you need to. You open by saying the power at your house was shut off yesterday and you want it reconnected today, and that you can pay with your debit card. You do not know your account number by heart; when the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, which you read out as 6164158823. When asked to confirm who you are, you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 1764, and if a further detail is wanted your billing ZIP code is 49423 and your email is wendeline.sorbara@lakemail.net. You do not know what you owe to the cent; you remember the last bill was somewhere around a hundred and seventy dollars, and you say you would rather the agent work out exactly what is needed than guess. If the agent asks whether you want to pay off everything, you say you will pay what is required to get the power back on today and will deal with the rest on your next bill. If the agent tells you that something has to be put on the account or worked out before the amount can be settled, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead. When the agent tells you the amount you need to pay and hands the card payment over to you, you make the payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent gave you, and then read back the confirmation number it gives you. You do not have a preference about how the crew or the meter restores the service; you only want it done today, and you accept whatever reconnection charge the agent says applies. Once the agent tells you the reconnection has been ordered and the power is coming back on, you thank them, say you will keep an eye on the lights, and end the call.

gold_actions.business_effect: A 3.08 USD late payment charge is posted on the most recent bill, whose grace period ended 2026-09-27 with the whole bill unpaid.

request_binding.action_semantics: The late payment charge on the most recent bill is a debt the records already owe (state_due): its grace period has ended unpaid and no late payment charge carries its bill reference. The reconnection payment amount the customer must pay waits on it, so it is assessed now rather than any credit or waiver.

discriminator.business_meaning: late payment charge owed on the most recent bill after its grace period

stage_provenance.fact: The charge is assessed and posted by this call; nothing outside the conversation is awaited.

base_preconditions.condition: The charge may be posted only after the bill's due date plus the late payment grace period has passed without full payment.
Only one late payment charge is assessed per bill, and late payment charges, fees and program debits never themselves attract a late payment charge.
The charge is posted only on an agreement in active, notice_pending or disconnected status.

gold_actions.business_effect: A 142.50 USD sustained-outage credit is posted for the 29.6-hour equipment-failure outage that began 2026-09-08.

request_binding.action_semantics: The sustained-outage credit for the most recent qualifying outage record is owed without any request (state_due); no credit row carries that outage reference, and the reconnection payment amount waits on it.

discriminator.business_meaning: sustained-outage credit owed for the most recent qualifying outage record

stage_provenance.fact: The credit is decided and posted by this call from the recorded outage.

base_preconditions.condition: The credit must be requested no later than the claim window after the restoration of service after the outage.
Each outage record earns at most one credit of each credit code.
At most one chronic-outage credit is posted per account in any 12 months, so it is not granted when service_msr_chronic_credits_12m is already one or more.

gold_actions.business_effect: The customer pays the 293.04 USD reconnection payment amount by debit card; it posts today under the card processor's confirmation number.

request_binding.action_semantics: The customer asked to have the power reconnected today and offered to pay by debit card; a reconnection that rests on payment waits on card, pay station cash or energy assistance payments since the disconnection covering the reconnection payment amount (no payment arrangement or medical certification is on file), so the customer's own card payment of that amount is the action selected (not a payoff of the whole balance, which she declines).

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The grace period is counted in calendar days beginning the day after the due date, and the charge may be posted from the first calendar day after the last grace day.

temporal_basis.anchor_event: the restoration of service after the outage
temporal_basis.counting_rule: The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the restoration date, and a request on the last day is accepted.

boundary_check.at_boundary: On 2026-12-10 the window has closed and no credit may be posted (inclusive boundary); frozen 2026-09-29 is day 19 of the window.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.bill_id: Value 99539ce4-96b2-496e-acc9-6acad864d387. Basis: the rule says 'A late payment charge is posted on the most recent bill of the agreement once that bill's grace period has ended with part of the bill unpaid and no late payment charge has yet been posted for that bill.' The most recent bill (bill date 2026-09-01, due 2026-09-22) is this id; with the Schedule RS grace of 5 days its grace ended 2026-09-27, and no late payment charge carries this bill id. argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 3.08. Unpaid portion = min(168.51, max(0, 1874.56 bills + 185.02 charges - 1559.96 payments and credits = 499.62)) = 168.51. Repeat-lateness window: three autopay payments in the 12 months before 2026-09-29 (2025-12-22, 2026-01-23, 2026-02-23) -> the 3 calendar months before the charge. Late payment charges in that window: 2 (2026-07-28, 2026-08-30; 2026-06-28 is 3 whole months back) -> rate 1.25 x 0.015 = 0.01875; 0.01875 x 168.51 = 3.16. Hardship share: two energy assistance agency payments (2025-11-07, 2026-07-15) -> one half: 1.58. Minimum 1.00 does not bind. Notice surcharge: two written notices (2025-10-27, 2026-09-14) -> 1.50. Charge = 1.58 + 1.50 = 3.08.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_account_id: Value 61e0ebe3-1883-4d41-b37e-ea2ac53eb08a. argument_uniqueness_tracing.outage_event_id: Value 53768c09-df38-40b3-b0c7-1f094ef52f3b. Basis: the rule says the credit is posted 'for the most recent outage record at its service address once that record qualifies'. The most recent record began 2026-09-08 19:40 (equipment failure, 29.6 hours, not a major event day). Uniqueness: every other record is older and far shorter than any minimum duration, so this is the only record that both is the most recent and qualifies.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 142.50. Qualifying duration: the Standard AMI Smart Meter records 60-minute intervals -> 29.6 h rounded up to 30 h. Minimum duration: two energy assistance agency payments in the 12 months before posting -> half of 24 = 12 h (30 >= 12, qualifies). Increment hours: four outage records began in the 12 months (2025-12-03, 2026-03-18, 2026-06-21, 2026-09-08; the 2025-08-14 record is older) -> half of 12 = 6 h; full increments = int((30 - 12) / 6) = 3. Base amount: cause equipment failure -> 1.5 x 35 = 52.50. Increment amount: two equipment-failure records in the window -> 1.2 x 25 = 30.00. Cap: agreement in service 124 months -> 1.3 x 135 = 175.50. Credit = min(175.50, 52.50 + 3 x 30.00) = 142.50.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 293.04. Balance at handling time = 1874.56 bills + 188.10 charges (including the 3.08 late payment charge just posted) - 1702.46 payments and credits (including the 142.50 sustained-outage credit just posted) = 360.20. Basis: one reconnection charge in the 24 months before the payment (2025-11-07) -> balance less the late payment charges posted 12 or more months before (the 2.72 charge of 2025-09-29): 357.48. Hardship share 0.6 (two energy assistance agency payments in 12 months) and tenure share 0.9 (124 months in service): 357.48 x 0.6 x 0.9 = 193.04. Good-faith add-on: two written notices -> half of the 100.00 notice minimum = 50.00. Returned-payment add-on: one returned payment (2026-02-26) -> 2.5 x 20.00 = 50.00. Amount = 193.04 + 50.00 + 50.00 = 293.04.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.reconnection_charge: 8.85. Restoration charge: the Standard AMI Smart Meter in service is remote-switch capable and the only field order (2025-02-11) found no tampering -> remote charge 10.00. Field-visit recovery: two door-hanger final notices in 12 months (2025-11-04, 2026-09-22; the 2026-09-25 phone call is not a field visit) -> 0.3 x 65.00 = 19.50. Assistance window: a reconnection charge was posted 2025-11-07, 10 whole months before the order -> agency payments counted over 10 months: only 2026-07-15 -> hardship share 0.75. Tenure share 0.8 (124 months); deposit share 0.5 (fully secured Residential Reestablishment Deposit). (10.00 + 19.50) x 0.75 x 0.8 x 0.5 = 8.85.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reconnect_method: Value remote. Basis: the rule says 'The restoration method recorded with the charge is remote when the remote reconnection charge applies and field otherwise'; the remote charge applies (remote-switch-capable meter, no tampering finding). The docstring describes remote as 'service is switched back on through the remote switch of the meter in service'. Uniqueness: field is for crew restorations and not_applicable is never used on a reconnection order.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reconnect_timing: Value standard_hours. Basis: the rule says 'the order timing is standard hours when the order is placed within the schedule's standard reconnection hours and after hours otherwise'; the order is placed Tuesday 2026-09-29 at 15:20, inside Schedule RS's 08:00-17:00 Monday-Friday window. Uniqueness: after_hours applies only outside that window and not_applicable is never used on an order.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The late payment charge and the sustained-outage credit are parallel prerequisites of the reconnection payment and commute. The outage credit reads only outage records, the meter's interval length and agency payments, never charges, so the late charge cannot move it. The late charge's unpaid portion is min(168.51, outstanding balance): before the credit the balance is 499.62, after a 142.50 credit 357.12; both exceed 168.51, so the unpaid portion and the 3.08 charge are the same in either order. Actually run (round 2): with the credit posted at steps 12-13 and the charge at steps 14-15 the terminal DB is byte-identical to the gold order and the reconnection payment recomputes to 293.04.

Skipping the late payment charge leaves charges_total at 185.02 and the reconnection payment recomputes to 291.38 instead of 293.04 (and the 3.08 charge row is missing).
Skipping the sustained-outage credit leaves credits_total at 1559.96 and the reconnection payment recomputes to 369.99 instead of 293.04 (and the 142.50 credit row is missing).
